title: Those grasping the burning coal
summary: Editorial on steadfastness, drawn from the hadith likening one who holds to his religion in the end times to a person clutching a live ember. It argues there is no route to salvation and constancy amid severe trials except by clinging firmly to the prophetic method, biting onto it and enduring its hardship. The piece marshals hadith on the reward of patience in adverse times, including the narration of al-Irbad ibn Sariya on holding to the Sunnah and the way of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs. It defines the correct path as tawhid, jihad by the sword, commanding right and forbidding wrong, proclaiming the truth, and loyalty and disavowal, and warns that laxity and compromise in creed lead to ruin. The editorial is doctrinal and hortatory, aimed at reinforcing endurance and discouraging defection or dilution of belief during a period it frames as intense fitna.
keyClaims: Salvation and steadfastness amid severe trials require clinging firmly to the prophetic method and enduring its hardship.
Patience in times of adversity carries immense reward, per the hadith of holding to religion like grasping a coal.
The correct path comprises tawhid, jihad, commanding right and forbidding wrong, and loyalty and disavowal.
Laxity and compromise in creed lead to ruin.
significanceAssessment: Doctrinal exhortation to endurance and resistance to ideological dilution, framed around end-times hadith on holding firm to faith. Functions to reinforce in-group cohesion and discourage defection or accommodation during a period IS characterises as intense fitna. Eschatological framing of perseverance is a recurrent feature of IS messaging on steadfastness.
notes: Editorial page only. Individual named is a historical Companion and hadith narrator. Hijri date (21 Shawwal 1447) converted to Gregorian 9 April 2026 and cross-checked against adjacent issues.
